title: A Locked Study Mystery
briefing: In a secluded country estate, the family attorney was found poisoned inside his private study bolted firmly from within. Five individuals were in the house, and one of them is guilty.

suspects.name: Charles Blackwood
suspects.publicStatement: I was playing billiards in the game room all evening.
suspects.background: Deep in debt, awaiting inheritance payout.

suspects.name: Beatrice Blackwood
suspects.publicStatement: I was in the music salon practicing piano preludes.

suspects.name: Edmund Finch
suspects.publicStatement: I was in the silver pantry polishing tableware.
suspects.background: Served the family for over thirty years.

suspects.name: Dr. Gregory Croft
suspects.publicStatement: I was reading medical journals by the fireplace in the library.
suspects.background: Longstanding confidant of the late patriarch.

suspects.name: Lucille Moreau
suspects.publicStatement: I was transcribing dictation rolls in the typing parlor.

clues.title: Billiard Table Felt Indentations
clues.description: Cold dust on the billiard felt reveals no balls were struck after 9:45 PM, contradicting Charles's alibi.
clues.insight: Dismantles Charles's claim of continuous solo billiard play.

clues.title: Pianola Mechanical Roll
clues.description: Sheet music and piano pedal logs confirm Beatrice was playing continuously during the crucial hour.
clues.insight: Exonerates Beatrice by confirming her whereabouts in the salon.

clues.title: Silver Polish Log and Cloths
clues.description: Drying rags and a full set of polished candelabras corroborate Finch's dedicated presence in the pantry.
clues.insight: Corroborates Finch's presence in the pantry throughout the evening.

clues.title: Physician Medical Bag Latch
clues.description: A brass vial cap from Croft's medicine case found near the fireplace.
clues.insight: Casts suspicion on Croft, but was dropped when he treated a burn earlier.

clues.title: Secretarial Steno Notebook
clues.description: Notes detailing Pendelton's intention to disinherit Charles, found in Lucille's desk.
clues.insight: Shows knowledge of the will change, but Lucille had no motive to execute the deed.

clues.title: Discarded Wine Decanter Cork
clues.description: A wine cork stained with port, pointing toward butler service.
clues.insight: Suggests Finch brought poisoned wine, but laboratory tests clear the decanter.

clues.title: Study Window Latch Thread
clues.description: A fine strand of monofilament fishing line looped around the sliding bolt from outside.
clues.insight: Reveals how the locked-room bolt was pulled shut from the terrace window.

clues.title: Tackle Box with Spool
clues.description: A spool of matching high-tensile line with fresh cut ends found hidden inside Charles's tackle box.
clues.insight: Connects Charles directly to the mechanism used to fake the locked room.

clues.title: Disinheritance Codicil Letter
clues.description: A formal notice signed by Pendelton revoking Charles's heirship due to gambling forgery.
clues.insight: Establishes urgent motive to murder Pendelton before the codicil was filed.

motive: To destroy the disinheritance codicil before it could be legally executed in the morning.
method: Administered poison in tea, exited through the window, and locked the interior bolt with monofilament line.
opportunity: Familiarity with the terrace window and fishing tackle allowed him to rig the locked room trick.

deduction.conclusion: Billiard table felt proves Charles vacated the game room during the poisoning window.
Monofilament line on the study window sill demonstrates the interior bolt was locked externally.
The matching spool in Charles's gun room and disinheritance notice prove his guilt and motive.

timeline.event: Charles leaves the billiard room and slips onto the north terrace.
Charles doses the tea and exits via the study window.
Charles pulls the sliding bolt shut using the monofilament trick.

hints.text: Inspect the billiard room felt for signs of active play.
Examine the exterior study window sill for foreign rigging materials.
Search the gun room for matching line spools and inheritance revocation notices.
